thesisInOneSentence: You can replace recurrence in sequence models with a single, simple mechanism — attention as a soft, parallel lookup — and get better results, faster.
audience: Anyone who's heard of neural networks but hasn't internalized self-attention. Assumes basic linear algebra and softmax familiarity.
hook: In 2017, eight researchers at Google quietly threw away the recurrence — and rebuilt sequence modeling around one idea.

narrativeArc.name: Why care?
narrativeArc.purpose: Hook: claim, paper title, the audacity of the idea.

narrativeArc.name: The setup
narrativeArc.purpose: What existed before (RNNs/LSTMs), why they were limiting, what we mean by Q, K, V.

narrativeArc.name: The core idea
narrativeArc.purpose: Build scaled dot-product attention from scratch, step by step.

narrativeArc.name: Why it works
narrativeArc.purpose: Why divide by sqrt(d_k); why softmax; intuition for parallel lookup.

narrativeArc.name: Implications
narrativeArc.purpose: What this paper unlocked. Closing card.

conceptsToVisualize.whyItMatters: Frames the central problem: sequential computation prevents parallelism and degrades long-range coupling.
conceptsToVisualize.visualSuggestion: manim — chain of dots passing a token left-to-right; highlight the long path from position 1 to position 100

conceptsToVisualize.concept: Q, K, V as soft database lookup
conceptsToVisualize.whyItMatters: Most viewers haven't internalized that attention is just a parametric lookup — once they have, the formula reads itself.
conceptsToVisualize.visualSuggestion: manim — show a query vector Q reaching toward keys K, the dot products as similarity scores, softmax normalizing, V values being mixed

conceptsToVisualize.whyItMatters: The headline equation. Must land cleanly.
conceptsToVisualize.visualSuggestion: equation card with stepwise reveal; Manim breakdown of each operation

conceptsToVisualize.whyItMatters: Paper hand-waves this. We must clarify: as d_k grows, dot-product variance grows; softmax saturates; gradients vanish. Scaling fixes it.
conceptsToVisualize.visualSuggestion: manim — bar chart of softmax outputs with and without scaling, showing one bar going to ~1.0 in the unscaled case

conceptsToVisualize.concept: all positions attend to all positions, in parallel
conceptsToVisualize.whyItMatters: Direct contrast to the recurrence bottleneck.
conceptsToVisualize.visualSuggestion: manim — fully-connected attention pattern animated as a square heatmap

questionsToAnswerOnScreen: Why does this work without any recurrence at all?
Where do Q, K, and V actually come from?
What does the softmax actually compute here?
Why divide by the square root of d sub k?
thingsToCutOrSkip: Multi-head attention (mention in passing only — out of 5-min scope).
Positional encoding details (mention as a one-line afterthought).
Position-wise feed-forward layers, layer norm, residuals (skip entirely).

priorWork.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
priorWork.whyRelevant: Set the encoder-decoder template that the Transformer disrupts.

priorWork.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
priorWork.whyRelevant: Introduced attention as a complement to RNNs — Transformer keeps the attention, drops the RNN.

narrativeAngles: Frame as: 'a soft, differentiable database lookup'.
Frame as: 'all positions can talk to all positions, at once' — the parallelism story.
criticisms: The paper hand-waves over why scaling is necessary — we MUST explain it (variance grows with d_k, softmax saturates).
Paper introduces multi-head before viewers grok single-head — we explain single-head only and mention multi-head as a one-line generalization.
